learning_objective: The learner will classify each of nine images as informative, decorative, or complex, with at least 8 of 9 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** image-type-sorter
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** classify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify each of nine images as informative, decorative, or complex, with at least 8 of 9 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Alt Text, Decorative Image, Complex Image Description (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each image the learner commits one of three bins. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct bin column in Content. Mastery is at least 8 of 9 correct on the first attempt. Reading the definitions is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Every image needs a long description. (2) A logo needs no alt text. (3) A decorative image should have alt text that says "decoration". **Instructional Rationale:** Classifying an image by its role is an Understand-level action that decides what kind of text it needs. Three images per type, each in a different setting, teach the learner to ask what the image does and not what it shows. **Content:** The three bins: Informative (needs short alt text), Decorative (needs empty alt text), Complex (needs short alt text and a long description or data table). The nine images: | # | Image shown to the learner (described in words) | Correct bin | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | A photo of a river with sharp bends, used to show how a river meanders. | Informative | It carries information the lesson uses, and a sentence can convey it. | | 2 | A thin decorative line between two sections. | Decorative | It adds no information. | | 3 | A bar chart of monthly rainfall with twelve bars. | Complex | The values need a table or a long description. | | 4 | A school logo in the page header that links to the home page. | Informative | Its alt text should state where the link goes. | | 5 | A stock photo of smiling students beside a heading, adding mood only. | Decorative | It carries no information. | | 6 | A labeled diagram of the water cycle with six labels and arrows. | Complex | The parts and the order of the arrows need a longer description. | | 7 | A screenshot showing which button to click in a software tool. | Informative | It shows where to click, and a sentence can say so. | | 8 | A map of a river and its tributaries with several labeled towns. | Complex | The places and their relations need a longer description. | | 9 | A small lightbulb icon beside the word "Tip" that the text already states. | Decorative | The adjacent text carries the meaning. | **Provenance:** The images are described in words for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The bins follow the chapter sections "Alt Text", "Decorative Image", and "Complex Image Description". **Rules:** Each image has exactly one correct bin, three per bin. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees a description of one image and the three bins. 2. The learner places the image in a bin, and the placement is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct, the Why text, and the kind of text the image needs. 4. After image 9 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 9 images in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [bin]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This is [bin]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 9 correct on the first attempt". At 8 or more it adds "You can tell which images need which text." Below 8 it lists the Why text of each missed image. **Starting State:** The first image description and the three bins. The question shown is "What does this image need?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says a decorative image takes an empty alt attribute, a complex image takes short alt text plus a longer description or table, and an informative image takes a short alt text.
